lawyer:
Ziaur Rahman Khan, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner. 
Habibul Islam Bhuiyan with Mirza Hossain Haider, Advocates ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Amirul Huq Shameem and others ----- Petitioners
Vs
AKM Shamsuddin & others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the judgment and order dated 22-3-1995 passed by the District Judge, Mymensingh in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 14 of 1995 allowing the prayer of the plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1-2 for temporary injunction restraining the petitioners and opposite party No. 3 (the Additional Secretary General, Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity) from disturbing the management of the affairs of the Executive Committee of Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Owners Association till disposal of the suit and further allowing the prayer for temporary mandatory injunction of the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 directing to restore to their status quo ante till 15-2-1995 and 19-2-1995 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 14 of 1995 (along with Miscellaneous Appeal No. 12 of 1995) and setting aside the order dated 9-2-95 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Mymensingh directing the parties to maintain status quo in OC Suit No. 19 of 1995. 

 2. It has been stated in the revisional application that the plaintiff opposite parties were members of the Executive Committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Owners Association and the said Executive Committee has remained virtually unaltered for the last 14 years with papers transaction showing Annual Elections. The last date of 'Elections' was on 6-8-1992 for a period of 2 years expiring on 5-8-1994. 

 9. It has been further stated in the revisional application that instead of handing over the duties and functions to the ad-hoc committee, the plaintiff respondent on 21-1-95 filed a declaratory suit before the Senior-Assistant Judge, Mymensingh being TS 19 of 1995 praying for the following relief 

 (a) a declaration that dissolution of Executive Committee of Mymensigh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity, and the appointment of an ad-hoc committee comprising defendant petitioners 2-10 by letter of defendant No. 1 dated 12-1-1995 is illegal and liable to be cancelled, and that plaintiffs are not bound by the same 

 (b) to restra tin the defendants 1 and 2 from interfering in the functions of committee by an order of permanent injunction. Along with this the plaintiff filed an application for temporary injunction. 

 10. The learned Sr. Assistant Judge having heard the plaintiffs was pleased to pass an order on 22-1-95 serving notice upon defendant-opposite parties asking them to show cause within 7 days as to why the order prayed for should not be granted, and in the meanwhile passed an order of ad interim injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with the working of the Executive Committee. 

 12.On 23-1-95 the defendant petitioners appeared and contested the matter by filing a written objection stating, inter alia, that plaintiffs have not made out an arguable prima facie case for injunction, that the balance of convenience is in favour of the defendants and against the plaintiffs inasmuch as the Executive Committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity headed by the plaintiffs had been dissolved at the instance of the defendant No.1 due to malpractice, mismanagement and high-handedness of the plaintiffs in running the affairs of the Association. The defendants further stated that the term of the Executive Committee had expired on 5-8-94 and no fresh elections had been called for or held even 6 months after the expiry of that period, and that the plaintiffs were ignoring the directives of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity and further there was even no constitution for Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Owners Association and no constitution could be given by committee whose term had expired 6 months earlier, and therefore, no such illegal committee could extend its own life with retrospective effect from 2 years to 3 years. And those arbitrary and high handed and unlawful acts of the plaintiffs have caused colossal damage to the spirit and image of the Samity and created an undesirable situation in the transport sector. And that at this juncture the President of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity (to which all other such transport samities are affiliated) along with others called an Emergency Meeting of the Central Committee on 19-1-1995 and after a thorough discussion upheld the spirit of the letter written by the defendant No.1, Additional Secretary General on 12-1-95 and resolved further that the ad-hoc committee had been legally constituted, that elections to the Executive Committee of the Samity will be held on 6-4-1995 under the supervision of the Central Committee under the circumstances the plaintiffs being no longer in the Executive Committee cannot seek equitable relief or obtain an injunction and hence the same should be dismissed. 

 16. The learned District Judge admitted the appeal against the order of status quo but rejected the prayer of the plaintiffs for temporary injunction in the followings words: 

 "By a petition they (Plaintiff appellants) now pray for temporary injunction. The order of status quo is also a sort of injunction in favour of the plaintiffs-appellants. I find no ground to issue an order of temporary injunction on the face of an order of status quo." 

 In course of the hearing the plaintiff respondents on 23-2-1995 put in 2 applications 

 18. The learned District Judge heard both the appeals together and disposed of the same by one order dated 22-3-95, setting aside the order of status quo, allowing the prayer for temporary injunction restraining the defendants from disturbing the plaintiffs in the management of the affairs of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity till disposal of the suit. The learned District Judge was further pleased to pass an order restoring the plaintiffs to their status quo ante till before 15-2-95 and 19-2-95 by an order of temporary mandatory injunction and ordered that the same order shall govern the fate of the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 12 of 1995. 

 21. Mr. Ziaur Rahman Khan has further submitted that the learned District Judge committed an error of law by allowing the prayer for temporary injunction even after the plaintiffs had withdrawn their application for temporary injunction on 23-2-95 and this has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice. 

 23. Mr. Khan has further submitted that the Executive Committee of the plaintiffs had no locus standi and the ad-hoc committee admittedly duly appointed by the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity was the lawful committee. 

 24. Mr. Khan has further submitted that the plaintiffs extended their committees with retrospective effect from 2 to 3 years, and this action was arbitrary, irregular, illegal and inequitable and hence the plaintiffs have disentitled themselves to the equitable remedy of injunction. 

 26. It has been further submitted that the impugned order suffers from non-application of judicial mind. Mr. Khan has also submitted that the plaintiffs have not come with clean hands and, as such, they are not entitled to an equitable relief. Mr. Khan has submitted that the balance of convenience is in favour of the defendant-petitioners. 

 28. Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2, by filing a counter affidavit has submitted that the Additional Secretary of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity has no lawful authority to dissolve the executive committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity and the plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 are duly elected President and Secretary of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity and the dissolution of the executive committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity by the Additional Secretary of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity is totally illegal and without any lawful authority and that being the position the courts below committed no illegality deciding the issue in favour of the plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1 and 2. 

 30. Mr. Bhuiyan also submitted that the Courts below reaching upon correct finding that the plaintiffs have a prima facie arguable case and, as such, there was no scope of interference in this Court in exercising its jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Mr. Bhuiyan submitted that the learned Court below committed no error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned order. 

 31. Mr. Bhuiyan has further submitted that the appellate Court has given reasons for passing an order of mandatory injunction. Mr. Bhuiyan has submitted that the plaintiffs are in management of the affairs of the committee. Mr. Bhuiyan lastly submitted that the Court has inherent power to pass an order of injunction. Mr. Bhuiyan in support of his contention has referred to 35 DLR (AD) 42 and has submitted that mandatory injunction on an inter-locutory application may be granted to restore the status quo and the Court has inherent jurisdiction to pass an order of mandatory injunction in a proper case. 

 32. I have heard both the parties at length, perused the application of the defendant petitioners and the counter affidavit on behalf of the plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 and the impugned judgments. 

 33. The plaintiff opposite parties filed a declaratory suit before the Senior Assistant Judge, Mymensingh being OC Suit No. 19 of 1995 (Title Suit No. 19 of 1995) for declaration that the dissolution of the executive committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity and the appointment of an ad-hoc committee comprising the defendant petitioners Nos. 2-10 by letter of defendant No. 1 dated 12-1-95 is illegal and liable to be cancelled and the plaintiffs were not bound by the same and to restrain the defendant Nos. 1 to 10 from interfering in the functions of the committee by an order of permanent injunction. Along with this the plaintiffs filed an application for temporary injunction. 

 36. Being aggrieved the defendants petitioners have preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge being Miscellaneous Appeal No.12 of 1995 along with an application for stay of the order of the Senior Assistant Judge. The plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No.14 of 1995 before the learned District Judge, Mymensingh along with an application for temporary injunction. 

 37. It appears that in the course of hearing the plaintiff opposite parties filed two applications a) praying for withdrawal of their petition for temporary injunction, b) praying for an order of mandatory injunction under Order 39, rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The prayer for withdrawal of the application for temporary injunction was allowed and the prayer for mandatory injunction was fixed for on 25-2-95. The application for mandatory temporary injunction of the plaintiffs was contested by the defendants by filing written objection. 

 38. The learned District Judge heard both the appeals together and disposed of the same by a single judgment dated 22-3-95, setting aside the order of status quo, allowing the prayer for temporary mandatory injunction restraining the defendants from disturbing the plaintiffs in the management of the affairs of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity till disposal of the suit. The learned District Judge was further pleased to pass an order restoring the plaintiffs to their status quo ante till before 15-2-95 and 19-2-95 by an order of temporary mandatory injunction. It is admitted that there was an executive committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity and it was headed by the plaintiffs respectively as the President and Secretary. 

 40. It is contended on behalf of the plaintiff opposite party Nos.1 and 2 that they are President and Secretary respectively of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity and that the Additional Secretary of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity has no lawful authority to dissolve the executive committee of Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity and it is further contended that the dissolution of the executive committee of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity by the Additional Secretary of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity is totally illegal and it has been contended that the life of the plaintiffs executive has been duly extended by the General Body of the Samity. It appears that the fight between the two sides is over the organisational functions and duties of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity, on the one side there is a committee of the plaintiffs opposite party Nos.1 and 2 and on the other side, the newly formed ad-hoc committee of which defendant No.2 is the convener. It appears from the revisional petition, para 8 that the convener of the newly formed ad-hoc committee (defendant No.2) wrote to the Chairman of the Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity requesting them to hand over the organisational duties and functions to ad-hoc committee at 10-30 AM on 21-1-95. That on the same date that is, 21-1-95, the plaintiff opposite parties filed a declaratory suit (OC Suit No.19 of 1995) for declaration that the dissolution of the executive committee was illegal. It appears that the executive committee of the plaintiffs claim themselves as the lawful committee as duly elected committee and their claim is that their life (the life of the plaintiff executive committee) has been lawfully and duly extended by the General Body of the Samity wherein 107 members including defendants No.2-10 were also present. 

 41. On the other hand, the convener of the newly formed ad-hoc committee (of the defendant No.2) claims to have the organisational duties and functions. The case of the defendant petitioners is that the term of the executive committee was over and the executive committee should hand over the organisational duties and functions to the ad-hoc committee and the unlawful acts of the plaintiffs in not doing so have caused colossal damage to the spirit and image of the Samity and created an undesirable and unbearable situation in the transport sector, and while the situation was such, the President and Secretary of the Bangladesh Sarak Paribahan Samity along with others called an Emergency Meeting of the Central Committee on 19-1-95 and after a full ledged discussion upheld the spirit of the letter written by the defendant No.1 and the ad-hoc committee has been legally constituted. 

 42. The learned Assistant Judge upon consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case finds in his judgment a prima facie arguable case in favour of the plaintiffs. On appeal the learned District Judge also found that the plaintiffs made out an arguable and prima facie case. The appellate Court found "since the plaintiffs are found to have made out an arguable and prima facie case for temporary injunction followed by an order of status quo on 9-2-95 any disturbance of theirs status quo ante till before 15-2-95 and 19-2-95 is to be restored". 

 46. It has been contended on behalf of the plaintiffs that defendant No.1 had not given the present executive committee a chance of being heard before dissolving their committee and, as such, natural justice has been denied to the plaintiffs by the defendant No.1. 

 47. Keeping in view of the facts and circumstances of the case both the Courts below found an arguable case in favour of the plaintiffs. 

 48. In view of the concurrent findings of the Courts below that the plaintiffs have a prima facie arguable case and multiplicity of proceedings are likely to be cropped up, I find that the suit itself should be heard expeditiously to avoid deterioration of the law and order situation concerning the associations of the parties. 

 49. I find that the learned District Judge acted within his inherent power and has rightly allowed the plaintiffs' prayer for temporary injunction and restraining the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 from disturbing the plaintiffs in the management of Mymensingh Dhaka Coach Malik Samity till disposal of the suit by the learned Assistant Judge.
